teams.heading: Stuart Barnes condemns RFU for extending Steve Borthwick's England contract
teams.body: Former England fly-half Stuart Barnes has launched a blistering attack on the Rugby Football Union, accusing the governing body of adopting an "ostrich policy" by extending Steve Borthwick's contract to 2028. Writing in his column, Barnes labelled England's recent campaign a "failure" following an embarrassing Six Nations loss to Italy and a heavy defeat to South Africa. Despite July victories over Fiji and Argentina, Barnes argued that Borthwick has turned the national side into a second-tier outfit, warning that the new deal is completely unjustifiable.

lead.why: Stuart Barnes' scathing criticism of the RFU's decision to extend Steve Borthwick's contract is the most significant and controversial talking point for England fans today.

teams.heading: IRFU dismisses World Rugby suggestions of playing Six Nations matches in US
teams.body: The Irish Rugby Football Union has ruled out taking Six Nations matches across the Atlantic, rejecting suggestions from World Rugby chief Alan Gilpin. Gilpin proposed Boston or New York as potential venues for an Ireland against Italy game to engage expatriate supporters. However, an IRFU spokesperson clarified there are "currently no plans or discussions" to relocate fixtures, asserting that playing at home remains central to the tournament's appeal. Italy's federation also rejected the idea.

lead.why: The IRFU's firm rejection of World Rugby's proposal to host Six Nations games in the United States is the day's dominant Irish rugby story.

teams.heading: Dave Butcher targets increased physicality after Scotland suffer 10-try Canada loss
teams.body: Interim head coach Dave Butcher faces a tough task to prepare Scotland for upcoming home tests against New Zealand and Australia after a chastening 64-26 defeat by Canada at Hive Stadium. Despite tries from Evie Gallagher, Shona Campbell, Lana Skeldon and Rhona Lloyd, the hosts were physically outmatched. teams.body: Argentina have struggled in defence over their last 11 matches, conceding a total of 346 points. Across that same 11-game window, the national side scored 321 points. teams.heading: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii resists calls to settle on one Wallabies position
teams.body: Wallabies utility back Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii has resisted pressure to lock down a permanent position ahead of next year's home Rugby World Cup, insisting he will maintain an "open mindset" regarding his role. The 23-year-old code-switcher has primarily featured at centre under head coach Les Kiss, but believes he can cover almost any backline position. Retired prop James Slipper urged Australia to prioritise getting him into space, but Kiss faces several selection conundrums before next year's tournament, including settling on his forward pack and captaincy.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One eligibility reforms stall after Timothy Lafaele settlement
teams.body: No further updates have emerged regarding Japan Rugby League One's eligibility restructure since last month's court settlement. The dispute was resolved in late August when the league settled a lawsuit filed by 24 foreign-born players, including World Cup centre Timothy Lafaele. While that agreement secured top eligibility status for players who gained Japanese citizenship before May 2025, officials have released no new updates on future intake categories before the competition kicks off in December.

teams.heading: Neil Barnes fumes at referee Karl Dickson after All Blacks Baltimore defeat
teams.body: All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes has criticised referee Karl Dickson's officiating during Saturday's 43-28 defeat to South Africa in Baltimore. The loss sealed a 3-1 series defeat, but Barnes argued the refereeing favoured the Springboks. He lamented that South Africa "kept getting penalties for bugger all" to slow down the game. Despite the result, Barnes remains confident in the squad's direction, insisting the All Blacks are close to the world champions' standard.

lead.why: Assistant coach Neil Barnes' highly critical post-match refereeing comments lead today's fallout from the series finale.

teams.heading: Damian de Allende scores twice as Springboks seal series victory in Baltimore
teams.body: South Africa wrapped up a 3-1 series victory over New Zealand on Saturday with a comprehensive 43-28 win in Baltimore. Damian de Allende scored in each half, while Morne van den Berg, Pieter-Steph du Toit, Kurt-Lee Arendse, and Cameron Hanekom also crossed. Despite a spirited All Blacks fightback that narrowed the deficit to eight points, Arendse's brilliant individual try from deep inside his own half extinguished any threat. The triumph in front of a packed American crowd solidifies the Springboks' status as World Cup favourites.

lead.why: South Africa secured a historic 3-1 series victory over the All Blacks with a dominant final-Test win.
